title: Finite family coefficient failure bound
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the Boolean cube, and let $\\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $[n]$. Let $\\varepsilon$ be a rational accuracy parameter in $(0,1/2]$, and choose any $S\\in\\mathcal F$. Draw uniformly an array of Boolean-cube samples indexed by $\\mathcal F$, with the sample count specified by $\\mathcal F$ and $\\varepsilon$. The probability that the empirical Fourier coefficient at $S$ differs from its true Fourier coefficient by at least the accuracy assigned to $\\mathcal F$ and $\\varepsilon$ is at most the confidence assigned to $\\mathcal F$.
hypotheses_covered: target is a sign-valued Boolean-cube function
